Our unified model surpasses harmonic extension across all evaluated families, including unseen cloth and legged bodies, without skeletons, registration, or cross-mesh correspondence. The same prior applies without retraining to point-tracked animal video and a robot grasping a soft body. Project page: https://su-terry.github.io/cepheid-website/

title: Urbex: Agentic Spatial Grounding for City-Scale 3D Scenes
abstract: City-scale 3D grounding is commonly formulated as candidate ranking, which requires precomputed instance proposals and becomes inefficient in large outdoor scenes. We propose Urbex, an agentic vision-language framework that instead casts grounding as active spatial search. Urbex represents a city-scale 3D scene as an interactive multi-view environment, allowing a VLM agent to query landmarks, zoom into local regions, render oblique views, and commit a grounded bounding box. We optimize this tool-use policy with reinforcement learning on CityRefer, using smooth localization rewards and lightweight shaping rewards for efficient exploration. Experiments show that Urbex achieves the best Hit@1 and IoU on CityRefer, supports candidate-free grounding without ground-truth boxes, and is substantially faster than the strongest city-scale ranking baseline. Zero-shot results on STPLS3D-Refer further indicate improved cross-scene robustness.

title: WAVE-0: Bridging VLA Policies and WAMs with Lightweight Latent Future Prediction
abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) policies excel at generalist robotic manipulation but generate actions without explicitly modeling their environmental consequences. World action models (WAMs) incorporate future prediction, yet most rely on costly video generation, while latent alternatives either use predicted futures only as auxiliary targets or infer latent actions from suboptimal visual transitions through costly large-scale video pretraining. We introduce WAVE-0 (World-model-Augmented VLA Execution), a framework that bridges VLAs and WAMs through a lightweight latent world model. By connecting the semantic understanding of pretrained VLAs with explicit future prediction, WAVE-0 allows anticipated action consequences to directly guide action generation. Built on a pretrained VLA, its 257M world model translates VLM-generated latent action plans into predicted future representations that condition the action expert, unifying latent planning, future prediction, and action generation. The world model is trained directly on ground-truth robot actions with a counterfactual ranking objective, requiring neither pixel reconstruction nor large-scale video pretraining. WAVE-0 achieves success rates of 91.47% on RoboTwin 2.0 and 98.7% on LIBERO, along with 88.0%, 61.4%, and 75.0% on LIBERO-Plus, LIBERO-Pro, and LIBERO-Para, respectively. On real-world tasks, it improves the success rate of π_{0.5} from 38.3% to 73.3%. These results demonstrate strong manipulation performance and generalization across diverse distribution shifts.

title: PsyBer-Agent: A Psychology-Driven User Agent for Recommender Systems
abstract: Evaluating recommender systems before deployment requires simulators that remain realistic over long, closed-loop interaction cycles. Current LLM-based agents generally function as surface imitators that generate realistic short-term responses but fail to capture the underlying user dynamics such as fatigue, affect, and shifting preferences. We propose PsyBer-Agent, a psychology-inspired simulator that models these dynamics through its Psy-Engine. This engine represents each user with three evolving, model-defined latent states. To calibrate simulated behavior against real interaction logs, we align log-conditioned reference trajectories with simulator-generated latent-state trajectories via Unbalanced Gromov--Wasserstein optimal transport. This approach provides structured supervision for a lightweight policy without the computational burden of fine-tuning the backbone LLM. We also introduce WebSim and the PsyBer Benchmark, which encompass multimodal scenarios and seven recommender backbones. Our framework evaluates behavioral fidelity, latent-state consistency, robustness, and responses to social-cue perturbations. On the tested horizons, PsyBer-Agent shows lower behavioral discrepancy than the prompt-only simulators while maintaining stable performance under large-scale concurrent simulation for up to 5M queued simulation tasks under bounded concurrency. Code is available in the supplementary material and at: PsyBer-Agent: https://anonymous.4open.science/r/CC66F/, WebSim Platform: https://anonymous.4open.science/r/D8EAX/.

title: ReTerm: Recovery Training for Self-Improving Terminal Agents
abstract: Terminal agents have shown strong abilities in complex coding tasks. However, they often struggle to recover from errors during long-running execution (e.g., command errors, faulty implementations), eventually leading to task failures. To this end, we present ReTerm, a self-improving terminal agent trained by learning how to recover from its own failed terminal tasks. To support its training, we construct a customized data pipeline and produce ReTerm-10K, a high-quality dataset that provides effective recovery demonstrations for SFT cold start. Furthermore, we propose ReTerm-GRPO, an online RL algorithm that forks from the agent's own failure states to generate multiple independent self-recovery attempts. By learning from whether these attempts successfully complete the task, the agent self-improves through its own recovery experience. Built on Qwen3.5-9B, our ReTerm-9B achieves 34.8% Pass@1 on Terminal-Bench 2.0, improving over the base model by 14.6 points. Further analysis shows that our method achieves consistently higher recovery rates across diverse error categories compared with standard GRPO training. All code, data and model are released at https://github.com/twothsnd/ReTerm.

title: Open-o3-Video-v2: Seek, Ground, and Reason with Verifiable Spatio-Temporal Evidence
abstract: Reliable video reasoning requires models to produce correct answers and expose supporting visual evidence. Open-o3-Video enables verifiable reasoning by embedding timestamps and object-level bounding boxes into reasoning traces, but is restricted to frames from an initial sparse sampler. We introduce Open-o3-Video-v2, which formulates video reasoning as a unified agentic evidencegrounded process. The model identifies missing information, acquires additional observations, grounds the moments and objects supporting its reasoning, and writes this evidence into the trajectory before continuing or answering. To support this behavior, we construct STGR-v2-CoT135K, including 52K multi-turn agentic grounded reasoning trajectories, and STGR-v2-RL-13K for reinforcement learning. We further propose Clue-Seek GRPO (CS-GRPO), which tracks how tool calls change accumulated evidence, rewards clue coverage and step-wise gains, and penalizes excessive, repetitive, or uninformative retrieval. On V-STaR, Open-o3-Video-v2-4B achieves 40.4% mAM and 56.3% mLGM, outperforming its Qwen3-VL-4B backbone by 8.5% and 12.6%, respectively. It also delivers consistent gains across general video understanding, long-video reasoning, and temporal grounding benchmarks. These results show that active evidence acquisition and verifiable object-level grounding are complementary for reliable video reasoning. The code and models are released at https://msalab-pku.github.io/projects/Open-o3-Video-v2.

title: Tev: Scaling Long-Horizon Agentic Environments with Dense Progress Rewards
abstract: Long-horizon agents have drawn growing attention for their ability to work autonomously -- from hours to days -- on economically valuable tasks, a capability essential to automated discovery and recursive self-improvement (RSI). Yet open-source models still struggle on long-horizon tasks, largely for lack of both training data and a working recipe, and scaling both is hard: long, complex tasks are difficult to curate and verify, and their rewards are sparse. We address both. First, we introduce Tev-Gym, the first long-horizon agent training dataset with verifiable, dense, progressive rewards -- 1,170 verified task environments across 7 domains. It is built on a latent-world-first approach that first constructs a latent world: a complete and correct hidden specification of the task domain, workflow, and expected state after each step. Each task is then progressively rendered from this specification into an agent-facing environment, enabling controllable complexity and a natural progress metric. Second, we turn this metric into a training recipe: via progress-potential reward shaping (PPRS), we convert progress into a dense per-step reward that improves training efficiency and makes otherwise-intractable tasks trainable. Training with this recipe yields Tev-27B, which achieves substantial gains on the Agents' Last Exam computing and math sciences domains (ALE-CM), matching GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5 at Pass@5. Despite training only on ALE-related data, it generalizes to the Terminal-Bench (TB) 3.0 and 4.0 subsets, surpassing GLM 5.2 and Gemini 3.7 Flash, and reaches Claude Opus 4.8-level performance on middle-horizon tasks such as TB 2.1.

title: uber/causalml v0.18.0
abstract: This release **deprecates positional `treatment` and `y`** ahead of the v1.0 switch to `fit(X, y, treatment, ...)`, makes **causal trees and forests estimate leaves honestly by default**, and moves the **uplift trees and forests onto the shared Cython tree kernel**, with native missing-value support. It also adds benchmark dataset loaders with ground-truth metrics, new CATE evaluation scores, model `save()` / `load()`, and a rebuilt [documentation site](https://causalml.readthedocs.io/en/stable/) with an end-to-end tutorial, an estimator guide and an FAQ. The full notes, with measurements, are in the [changelog](https://causalml.readthedocs.io/en/stable/changelog.html). ## ⚠️ Breaking Changes * **`BaseSLearner.estimate_ate` always returns `(ate, lb, ub)` and no longer accepts `return_ci`.** `ate = learner.estimate_ate(...)` now binds a tuple, and passing `return_ci` raises `TypeError`; unpack instead: `ate, lb, ub = learner.estimate_ate(...)`. By @su-jin1425 in https://github.com/uber/causalml/pull/1031 ## Deprecations * **Positional `treatment` and `y` emit a `FutureWarning` (#854).** In v1.0 the positional order becomes `fit(X, y, treatment, ...)`, the scikit-learn convention. Pass both by keyword — `learner.fit(X=X, treatment=treatment, y=y)` — which is correct before and after the flip. A call left positional will silently train on swapped arguments at v1.0 rather than raise. See the [migration guide](https://causalml.readthedocs.io/en/stable/migration.html). By @jeongyoonlee in https://github.com/uber/causalml/pull/975 ## Behavior Changes These change fitted models or estimates without any edit to your code. * **`CausalTreeRegressor` and `CausalRandomForestRegressor` default to `honesty=True`**: the tree structure is grown on one half of the sample and leaf values are re-estimated on the other ([Athey & Imbens 2016](https://arxiv.org/abs/1504.01132)). Pass `honesty=False` for the previous behavior. By @jeongyoonlee in https://github.com/uber/causalml/pull/1001 * **The default propensity models produce different scores**: log-loss model selection over a wider `C` grid for the logistic models, `max_depth=3` (was 8) for `GradientBoostedPropensityModel`, and a seeded, stratified early-stopping split. By @arpitjain099 in https://github.com/uber/causalml/pull/944, @su-jin1425 in https://github.com/uber/causalml/pull/1033 and @ismailvc1111 in https://github.com/uber/causalml/pull/1051 * **`UpliftTreeClassifier` and `UpliftRandomForestClassifier` run on the shared tree kernel.** Names, arguments and output shapes are kept; `X_val` / `treatment_val` / `y_val` and `early_stopping_eval_diff_scale` are ignored with a `UserWarning` (use `prune_fraction` instead), and `DecisionTree` is deprecated. By @jeongyoonlee in https://github.com/uber/causalml/pull/973 * **`UpliftRandomForestClassifier` defaults to `n_jobs=None`** (was `-1`), because peak memory grew with the core count. Predictions are unchanged; pass `n_jobs=-1` to restore. By @jeongyoonlee in https://github.com/uber/causalml/pull/992 * **`causalml.features.load_data` returns `numpy.ndarray` instead of `numpy.matrix`**, and no longer raises when the one-hot encoder produces no columns. By @arpitjain099 in https://github.com/uber/causalml/pull/978 and https://github.com/uber/causalml/pull/979 ## New Features * Benchmark dataset loaders (`fetch_lalonde`, `fetch_ihdp`, `fetch_twins`), ground-truth metrics (`pehe`, `ate_error`, `policy_risk`) and a reproducible leaderboard notebook by @jeongyoonlee in https://github.com/uber/causalml/pull/1015 * `ccp_alpha="cv"` on the causal tree: cost-complexity pruning with the tree size chosen by cross-validation by @jeongyoonlee in https://github.com/uber/causalml/pull/1001 * `pretrain=True` on `CausalTreeRegressor.estimate_ate` and `BaseDRIVLearner.estimate_ate` by @jeongyoonlee in https://github.com/uber/causalml/pull/1024 * `prune_fraction` on `UpliftTreeClassifier` for validation-based pruning inside `fit` by @jeongyoonlee in https://githu
